models._description: Synchronize a record with Google Calendar (AbstractModel mixin)

behavioral_notes.observation: OAuth2 authorization-code flow against Google. GoogleCalendarService._google_authentication_url builds the consent URL via google.service._get_authorize_uri for scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar with access_type=offline and approval_prompt=force (so Google returns a refresh_token). Google redirects back to the /google_account/authentication controller, which POSTs the code to https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/token via _get_google_tokens to exchange it for access_token + refresh_token + ttl; these are stored on res.users.settings (google_calendar_rtoken/token/token_validity, group base.group_system, blacklisted from session_info). _get_google_calendar_token lazily refreshes an expired access token (validity < now+1min) by POSTing the refresh_token to the same token endpoint; on 400/401 (invalid_grant) it wipes the stored tokens and commits. None of this token lifecycle is visible from field/model metadata.

Bidirectional sync. _sync_google_calendar pulls remote events (GoogleCalendarService.get_events -> GET https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/primary/events), then (Google->Odoo) calls calendar.recurrence/calendar.event._sync_google2odoo to create/update/cancel Odoo records, and (Odoo->Google) calls _sync_odoo2google on records returned by _get_records_to_sync (those with no google_id or need_sync=True, capped at 200/transaction). Conflict resolution is last-updated-wins: _sync_google2odoo parses each gevent.updated and only writes the Odoo record if updated >= the record's stored write_date. _sync_odoo2google routes each record to _google_insert (POST), _google_patch (PATCH) or _google_delete (DELETE) against the v3 events API. Deleting an Odoo event archives it instead of hard-deleting (a Google-linked event must survive so the deletion can be propagated at next sync). This cross-system create/update/delete reconciliation is pure runtime behavior absent from metadata.

Odoo->Google writes are deferred to post-commit. The @after_commit decorator registers the API call on cr.postcommit so the outbound HTTP request to Google fires only after the Odoo transaction commits (with a fresh cursor/registry), preventing an event from being created in Google when the Odoo write later rolls back (avoids duplicates after a crash). The no_calendar_sync context key short-circuits sync entirely. On a 400/403 HTTPError the record is flagged need_sync=False and an explanatory note is posted to the event chatter (_google_error_handling, subtype mail.mt_note) so a broken event stops retrying. The transactional-boundary coupling and error-to-chatter side-effect are not metadata-derivable.

behavioral_notes.element: incremental sync token (google_calendar_sync_token / nextSyncToken) + InvalidSyncToken full-sync fallback
behavioral_notes.observation: Polling delta-sync, not a push webhook. get_events sends the stored google_calendar_sync_token as Google's syncToken so only events changed since the last run are returned; the response's nextSyncToken is persisted back on res.users.settings. When the token is absent (first run) a full sync is performed, bounded to +/- google_calendar.sync.range_days (default 365) around now via timeMin/timeMax. If Google returns 410 fullSyncRequired the token is treated as expired (InvalidSyncToken raised) and a full sync is forced. There is NO Google push/watch channel: syncs are driven by the cron ir_cron_sync_all_cals (res.users._sync_all_google_calendar, every 12h, commits per user) and on-demand by the /google_calendar/sync_data route. The token-based windowing and full-resync fallback are runtime-only.

Outbound HTTPS integration via python-requests to two Google hosts (host allow-listed by assertion in google.service._do_request): accounts.google.com (OAuth auth + token endpoints) and www.googleapis.com (Calendar v3 REST: events list/get/insert/patch/delete on calendars/primary). Auth is per-user OAuth2 access_token (Bearer header or access_token param); the admin supplies google_calendar_client_id (public, in clear) and google_calendar_client_secret (ir.config_parameter, masked in logs). No vendored SDK -- the REST client is hand-rolled in utils/google_calendar.py + google_account/models/google_service.py. This external SaaS dependency is invisible to Python model/field metadata and is the defining trait of the module.

classification.rationale: google_calendar is calendar-sync integration infrastructure: it adds no business object of its own (only a sync-state mixin google.calendar.sync, a settings/token extension and a reset wizard) and produces no sellable output. It is a connector that extends the calendar subsystem by wiring Odoo's calendar.event/recurrence to an external SaaS (Google Calendar v3) over OAuth2 + REST. Per Stabell & Fjeldstad this is a support / firm-infrastructure function (activity_class=support). For APQC it maps to 8.0 Manage Information Technology -- specifically the 'manage IT integration / data interoperability' band: the module's whole reason to exist is external-system integration (gap #7, talks to googleapis.com and accounts.google.com), OAuth credential lifecycle management and cross-system data reconciliation, which are IT-management concerns rather than business-capability development. This is the deliberate point of departure from its parent calendar.metamodel.json (classified 13.0 Develop and Manage Business Capabilities, i.e. the collaboration/scheduling capability itself): the parent owns the scheduling capability; this child owns the IT plumbing that integrates that capability with a third-party service, which is exactly what 8.0 covers. 13.0 was considered (inherited from the parent) but rejected because nothing here develops a new business capability -- it operates an external interface; 9.0 'Acquire, Construct, and Manage Assets' was also rejected since no physical/IT asset is managed, only an API connection.

standard_capabilities: OAuth2 connect to a Google account (offline access + refresh token)
two-way sync of events and recurrences between Odoo calendar and Google primary calendar
incremental delta sync via nextSyncToken with automatic full-resync on token expiry
background sync cron (12h) plus on-demand sync from the calendar view
per-user pause / stop / restart and an account-reset wizard (delete in Google/Odoo/both)
typical_fits: internal users mirroring their Odoo meetings to personal Google Calendar
self-hosted Google Cloud project: admin sets client id/secret in Settings
last-updated-wins reconciliation for occasional concurrent edits
common_gaps: no Google push/watch webhook -- latency bounded by the 12h cron unless the view triggers sync
syncs only the primary calendar; secondary/shared Google calendars are not supported
full-sync window hard-bounded to +/- range_days (default 365); older/farther events excluded
no field-level merge -- whole-event last-writer-wins can drop concurrent edits to other fields
birthday and non-primary eventType events are filtered out
drive_hints: odoo shell: env['res.users']._sync_all_google_calendar()  # run the cron sync for all connected users
